Tessa / Karthik — quick draft below for external consumption. Marissa: please add legal caveats.

Suggested response for procurement:  
- Redwood retains billing artifacts (invoices, aggregated usage ledgers, charge IDs) for legitimate business needs including accounting, tax, and audit obligations.
- Per our retention schedule, invoice and ledger entries are retained for a minimum of 7 years to satisfy US accounting and tax recordkeeping requirements, unless a narrower timeframe is required by specific country-level laws.
- When a data erasure (DSR) is requested for a user profile, we will remove personal identifiers from operational product logs where feasible; however, we maintain a separate billing ledger and invoice records that are kept as necessary to meet financial and legal obligations. Any such ledger entries are treated as accounting records and are not typically considered part of the live profile data covered by user-facing erasure.

Quick notes:  
- We should call out that we can pseudonymize or redact personal identifiers in billing entries on a case-by-case basis if requested and if it won't break accounting/audit trails.
- If Finch has a statutory requirement that conflicts with our standard retention schedule, we should route to legal for an exception assessment.

I'll attach the summary and the retention matrix.

Thanks Neha — adding the legal framing (short):

- Invoices and ledger entries constitute accounting records necessary for statutory reporting and anti-fraud controls; as such, they fall under a narrow exception to erasure obligations in many jurisdictions. We should state this clearly but avoid overpromising — e.g., say "we retain billing records as required by law and for legitimate accounting purposes" rather than an absolute timeframe in the customer-facing line.
- Recommended customer-facing paragraph (one-liner): "Redwood retains billing and invoicing records as necessary for accounting, tax, and audit obligations. Personal identifiers used solely for billing purposes may be redacted or pseudonymized where doing so does not conflict with legal or financial requirements; please contact your procurement or account team to discuss options."
- If a customer requests full removal of invoice-level data tied to a specific charge, we need a documented legal/finance review to assess (a) statutory obligations, (b) downstream accounting impacts, and (c) whether an alternative (pseudonymization) satisfies the request.

Karthik — can you confirm if we need to add any specifics for multi-tenant EU customers re: local VAT invoicing rules? Also flag any Marketplace/partner billing exceptions.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
